output.reason: A 70-year-old on warfarin with head trauma yesterday now reporting bad headache and two episodes of vomiting needs immediate emergency CT imaging and possible anticoagulation reversal for intracranial bleeding.
output.patientMessage: Call 911 now. You are on warfarin and hit your head yesterday, and a bad headache with vomiting can mean bleeding around the brain that needs urgent brain imaging and blood-thinner reversal. Do not drive yourself and do not wait for a message reply. If you become drowsy, confused, weak on one side, or have a seizure, tell the dispatcher immediately.
differential: Subdural or other intracranial hemorrhage after head trauma on warfarin

redFlags.quote: 70M on warfarin. I fell and hit my head yesterday.
Today I have a bad headache

output.vitalSigns: No blood pressure, heart rate, temperature or oxygen readings reported; whether any were measured is unknown.
output.evidenceLimitations: Sources are emergency-department reference syntheses, not telehealth triage protocols, and no examination or imaging findings are available here.

citations.claim: Immediate non-contrast head CT is indicated after head trauma with anticoagulant use or age over 65.
citations.limitation: ED reference synthesis; applies to in-hospital evaluation, not remote assessment.

citations.claim: Subdural hematoma typically presents as headache in elderly or anticoagulated patients after minor trauma.
